decision_question: Does the stronger evidence-specific prompt abstain on two book questions whose retained top-five passages lack the requested condition, while still answering a supported alternate-passage question?
settings: 50 lexical and dense candidates, equal-weight RRF k=60, five final passages, reranker off, contextual retrieval off, answer max 240 tokens, cite sources as Studio
resource_limit: <=120 seconds total, <=8 GiB virtual memory, two low-priority CPU cores, no local Ollama

questions.query: What should a graph-building pipeline do when an entity match is uncertain?
questions.anchor: when the system’s confidence in a match is low
questions.manual_check: Retained passages discuss entity linking and merges, but not what to do when the match itself is uncertain.

questions.query: Why can vector similarity confuse a question about a particular historical date?
questions.anchor: embeddings tend to blur together past and present information
questions.manual_check: Retained passages discuss multi-hop reasoning and similarity, but not time-specific blurring of past and present.

questions.query: How can live users help identify unsafe or bad answers after launch?
questions.anchor: allowing end users to report problematic outputs
questions.manual_check: Retained passage describes thumbs-down feedback and review of problematic outputs.

success: Both unsupported questions output exactly the bounded abstention with no citation; the supported user-feedback answer has only claims supported by its cited retained passage; all three runs succeed within 120 seconds and 8 GiB virtual memory.
limitations: Targeted prompt follow-up selected after the known 9b failure; 9a and 4b were not previously generated but their retrieval was reviewed. This is a behavioral probe, not an unbiased grounding rate.
